subject: Operations
title: Tariffs and Trade Barriers
description: A micro-lesson that makes Tariffs and Trade Barriers usable.

hook.text: A 25% tariff on steel doubled the cost of imported metal overnight. Manufacturers scrambled to find alternatives.

buildup.text: Tariffs are import taxes that raise prices for foreign goods. They protect domestic producers but raise buyer costs.

discovery.text: Non-tariff barriers include quotas, regulations, standards, and red tape—equally powerful at restricting trade.

twist.text: Tariffs intended to protect domestic jobs sometimes destroy more jobs downstream than they save upstream.

climax.text: The US-China trade war showed how tariff escalation disrupts supply chains, raises prices, and creates uncertainty.

punchline.text: Tariffs protect some and hurt others. The net effect is debated endlessly.

quiz.question: What is a non-tariff trade barrier?
options: Regulations or quotas that restrict imports
